delta.comment: AFFECTED BY OPEN P1 (F18) — RECONCILE THE TRANSITION TABLE BEFORE IMPLEMENTING. This task's linear state summary omits required transitions: LOCKING -> REFUSED, the bootstrap/resolve/launch failure edges to FAILED, and RESTARTING -> LAUNCHING. Because absent transitions must raise ILLEGAL_TRANSITION, implementing the summary verbatim would reject documented outcomes. Additionally, Plan section 3.2's diagram routes operator cancellation CANCELLING -> EXITED, bypassing DRAINING, which contradicts the prose rule immediately below it (DRAINING is the ONLY path from RUNNING to a terminal state and always flushes the journal, releases the lock, and reaps the child) and contradicts 119.006-T, which mandates RUNNING -> CANCELLING -> DRAINING -> EXITED. Implementing the diagram as drawn would leak the workspace lock and the child process and lose journal data on every cancellation. The correct resolution is low-ambiguity: the diagram is the outlier; route cancellation through DRAINING and complete this task's table against Plan section 3.2. Recorded OPEN rather than applied because the 3-cycle plan-review budget is exhausted and this is a plan-document amendment. This task is in 128-S, so the finding does not block 127-S, but must be dispositioned before 128-S is claimed. See docs/reviews/2026-08-09-copilot-cli-supervisor-control-plane-review.md (Cycle 4, F18).

This task requires session.py to emit SessionPhaseChanged, but that event type is not defined until 119.004-T, whose dependency edge points BACK to this task (119.004-T -> 119.003-T, confirmed in the live graph). BLOCKING — F22 (P1, OPEN, NEW, raised by the tenth PR #325 Copilot review of HEAD 914cb214, AFTER the 3-cycle plan-review budget was exhausted). DO NOT IMPLEMENT THIS TRANSITION TABLE AS SPECIFIED UNTIL THE OPERATOR RULES.

DEFECT: plan §3.2 routes THREE failure edges directly to FAILED, all of them AFTER `LOCKING` has already succeeded — `BOOTSTRAPPING —(fatal)→ FAILED`, `RESOLVING —(no copilot exe)→ FAILED`, and `LAUNCHING —(spawn error)→ FAILED`. None passes through `DRAINING`. Rule 2 of the same section scopes the cleanup guarantee narrowly — DRAINING "is the only path to a terminal state FROM RUNNING" — and DRAINING is where the plan places journal flush, LOCK RELEASE and child reaping. So on this plan every pre-RUNNING failure terminates while still holding the workspace lock.

WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT COSMETIC: plan §3.4 makes the leak durable rather than transient — "Lock contention → REFUSED (never auto-break). Stale lock (dead PID / mismatched start-time) requires an explicit operator --force-unlock." The fail-closed stale policy is correct in isolation; combined with the missing cleanup edges it converts an ordinary failure into a PERSISTENT SELF-INFLICTED LOCKOUT of the operator's own workspace. And the triggering edge is the most likely first-run outcome there is: `RESOLVING —(no copilot exe)` fires on any machine where the Copilot CLI is not on PATH. The plan's most probable first failure locks the workspace, and every retry then fails with REFUSED until the operator discovers an undocumented --force-unlock.

RELATED SCOPE NOTE: 118.005-T (T5, locking.py) owns the lock lifecycle and sits in 127-S. If the operator places the guaranteed-release obligation on T5 (e.g. scope-guarding acquisition so release is structural rather than dependent on the caller reaching DRAINING), the fix touches the FIRST shipment, not just this one.

ALSO SEE F18 and F23 on this same task/state machine. All three are symptoms of one missing invariant: cleanup and cancellation are guaranteed only from RUNNING. A single operator ruling — "once LOCKING succeeds, EVERY terminal exit routes through DRAINING, and operator cancel is legal from EVERY post-LOCKING phase" — discharges all three and makes Rule 2 unconditional.

STAGE ADOPTED NO RESOLUTION and changed no dependency edge. Detail: docs/reviews/2026-08-09-copilot-cli-supervisor-control-plane-review.md (Cycle 4, tenth Copilot pass).
